stories.title: Data suggest a shift in the approach to Alzheimer’s disease prevention and treatment is warranted
stories.description: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is affecting millions of aging people in the USA and around the world. Especially in the USA, intense efforts have been directed towards developing drugs that might address the Amyloid Hypothesis. But these efforts have proved to be disappointing, with poor efficacy and serious side effects. Moreover, questions continue to be raised regarding the validity of key published data. This approach has largely undervalued the possible contribution of vasoconstriction and hypertension to AD onset and progression. There are many safe drugs currently used to treat hypertension, but their possible relevance to prevent or treat AD has received little attention. There are data in medical records and in clinical trials already documented that indicate vasodilator drugs might have a preventive or even therapeutic role in treating AD. If cheap, already approved drugs were shown to be effective, the implications for healthcare costs could be enormous.

stories.title: Association of the planetary health diet index with overweight and obesity among patients with diabetes mellitus in a cross sectional study
stories.description: The Eat-Lancet diet, which encourages a shift towards plant-based foods and reduced intake of animal products, has been proposed as a solution to improve both human health and environmental sustainability. This study explores the association between Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI) adherence and the risk of overweight or obesity in type 2 diabetes (T2D) residing in Tehran, aiming to determine whether this diet can serve as a dual-purpose strategy for managing weight and promoting planetary health. A total of 210 participants were recruited in this cross-sectional study. Dietary information was gathered via a validated 168-item food frequency questionnaire, and PHDI score was derived from 16 food groups. Anthropometric assessments were performed following standard procedures to identify overweight or obesity. Associations between PHDI and outcomes were examined using logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models. Study participants had a mean age of 62.15 ± 8.60 years, and 70% were female. PHDI was categorized into tertiles, with 33.3% of individuals in the highest tertile. In fully adjusted logistic models, high PHDI adherence was associated—though not significantly—with lower odds of overweight/obesity (OR: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.42, 1.95) and obesity (OR: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.37, 2.20) compared to low adherence. Additionally, we did not observe any non-linear association between PHDI and odds of overweight/obesity in T2D patients, after adjustments for potential confounders. Given the absence of a statistically significant link between PHDI and the likelihood of overweight or obesity, which may reflect insufficient statistical power, future studies incorporating larger cohorts and diverse populations are needed to assess the generalizability of these findings.
